newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: French ministers visit riot-torn Guiana.
newsitem.headline: French ministers visit riot-torn Guiana.

text.p: France rushed two cabinet ministers to French Guiana on Tuesday after organised gangs of armed rioters looted and torched stores in the wake of student protests.
"We are here to listen to all of (French) Guianese society. Our method is to listen with respect," France's education minister Francois Bayrou told reporters in the capital Cayenne.
Bayrou said he would meet student groups later on Tuesday as well as a broad spectrum of French Guianese society.
" I haven't arrived with prefabricated solutions, we have come to listen," he added.

The riots were sparked by a strike of high school students protesting at poor conditions in local schools. Protests were soon overtaken by more radical groups, some of whom favour French Guiana's independence from Paris.
Paris has sent more than 500 paramilitary riot police reinforcements to this city of 35,000.
Overseas Departments Minister Jean-Jacques de Peretti has blamed the violence on failure by the previous Socialist government to increase the number of teachers in line with a population boom.
"Fifty percent of the population is less than 25 years old. More jobs must be created every year, this is extremely difficult," de Peretti said.

One person died and at least 20 were injured during four nights of rioting last week in Cayenne. The violence caused millions of dollars in damage to property -- mostly government buildings and shops.
Government representative Pierre Dartout has described the riots as "planned actions by organised groups who aim to destabilise Guiana".
He said many of the rioters were foreign nationals.
Illegal immigrants, mostly from Haiti, Brazil and neighbouring Surinam make up about a quarter of the population of 150,000. More than 8,000 of the total population receive French welfare payments.

The immigrants were lured to French Guiana during a growth period in the late 1980s and early 1990s, triggered in part by construction at the European Space Agency launch site in Kourou and some dam projects.
French Guiana, located in northern South America and in French hands since the 17th century, is the only non-independent territory remaining on the continent.
